text:
tess: Heads-up — bringing up Shoreline customer's LFA adapter (merge #512) into staging. Adapter uses adapter_blocks.v2 and tokenmap shore2. Quickpack scope: invoice ids, thousands separators, percentages, and UK/US locale dates. Running int4 smoke + int8-hybrid for contrast. Posting quick hits here.

omar: Thanks. Do we have a conversion step for shore2 -> base token ids or relying on loader alias? Also are there renamed special tokens?

tess: shore2 renamed <PCT> -> <percent_sign> and swapped a few currency tokens. No conversion shipped yet; runtime supports --adapter-alias flag but it's opt-in per adapter.

leon: Ran 400-sample quickpack on shoreline-lfa:v1 int4. Topline: invoice-id EM -1.1% vs baseline, percentage recognition down 2.5pts. Example: 
```
input: "Discount: 12.5%"
baseline: "12.5 percent"
shoreline-lfa:int4: "125 percent"
```
Looks like the decimal and percent tokenization collapsed. Also thousands separators cause odd parses: "1,200" -> "120000" in a few cases.

tess: yikes. Can you re-run with --no-fast-bpe and --kv-cache on? Command we use: 
```
r-infer eval --model shoreline-lfa:v1 --quant int4 --prompts quickpack_financials_shore.json --no-fast-bpe --kv-cache on --out /tmp/shore_int4_kv.json
```
Also run int8-hybrid for baseline comparison.

ci-bot: Canary created for shoreline-lfa:v1 -> id 66002. 8k tokens queued, p50 69ms, p95 205ms. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/canaries/66002

tokenizer-bot: token-diff requested between base_tok and shore2_tok. Running python tools/token_diff.py... will post CSV.

omar: If decimal/commas are token-id shifts we should try adapter_alias=true first. If alias fixes >80% we'll bake it into loader for adapter_blocks.v2. If not, produce a minimal map patch.

leon: Re-ran with adapter_alias=true + no-fast-bpe. Decimal collapse mostly fixed, percentage recovery ~+1.9pts but thousands-separator bug still present in about 9 examples. Sample: 
```
input: "Subtotal: 1,200.00"
baseline: "1200.00 USD"
shoreline-lfa:int4+alias: "120000.00 USD"
```
So comma token seems mapped to a digit-group token now being interpreted differently in decode.

tokenizer-bot: token_diff output: /tmp/tokdiff_shore_66002.csv. Findings: shore2 has merged tokens for ","+digits (e.g., ",200") into single token id 9834 whereas base splits "," and "200". Also <percent_sign> id differs.

tess: That mapping explains both failures. Omar, can you craft an alias mapping that splits ",200" -> "," + "200" for common groupings or map shore2[",200"] -> base[",200"] where possible? Prefer minimal patch that preserves Shoreline's custom tokens for other uses.

omar: I'll try a minimal alias that remaps the merged thousand-group tokens to their split equivalents for the most common group sizes (3 and 6 digits). Prototype command: 
```
python tools/make_alias.py --tok-diff /tmp/tokdiff_shore_66002.csv --out /tmp/shore_alias.json --groups 3,6
```
If prototype closes >75% failures we push to staging.

leon: Also ran int8-hybrid with alias: int8-hybrid recovered nearly fully (percentage+thousands fixed). That suggests quant grouping amplifies the merged-token decode issue. Good to have int8 as control.

ci-bot: Canary 66002 update: preliminary run with alias applied - errors dropped from 0.9% -> 0.26%. p50 71ms. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/shoreline/66002

tess: Great. But we need to be careful: alias may mask other regressions. Plan: (1) run full quickpack sweep with alias + no-fast-bpe, (2) if pass, schedule quant-resweep (gptq group 128->64 and try alpha=0.9/1.0), (3) add quickpack_financials_shore to long-term regression suite (shoreline-reg-v1).

omar: I'll push alias prototype to staging and kick another canary. Also will add targeted unit tests for comma-group tokens to tokenizers CI.

leon: One more note: a few date formats (e.g., 03/04/24) still flip day/month. Might be a locale token mapping issue vs model behavior. I'll isolate date prompts and rerun to see whether it's tokenizer or model-level preference.

tokenizer-bot: Additional token-diff artifacts uploaded: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/shoreline/66002/tokdiff.zip

tess: Owners: @tess (owner), @omar (tokenizer), @leon (eval). If alias closes >80% and quant-resweep looks stable we'll consider staged rollout; otherwise we'll block. Reactions: :eyes: :shipit: 

leon: Uploaded failure CSV and top 50 examples to the artifact store for triage. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/shoreline/66002/failures.csv

omar: Prototype alias in staging, starting canary run now.

ci-bot: Canary 66002 second run started. 12k tokens scheduled. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/canaries/66002/run2

tess: Thanks all — will monitor. If decimal/thousand parsing resurfaces after wider canary we'll rollback and reopen thread.
